steps.label: The definition
lines: The reaction quotient Q has the same
expression as the equilibrium constant Kc,
but the concentrations in it are the values
at ANY moment of the reaction, not only at
steps.why: Kc is fixed for a given temperature, but Q changes as the reaction runs — the single difference between the two is WHEN the concentrations are measured.
common_mistakes: Writing a different expression for Q. The expression is identical to Kc; only the moment of measurement differs.
Calling Q a constant. Q changes as the reaction proceeds.
steps.memory_tip: Same fraction, different moment: Kc at equilibrium, Q at any time.
steps.margin_note: The words 'at any moment' are the definition.

If Q > Kc, the reaction proceeds in the

lines.text: Q = Kc means the system is at equilibrium

steps.why: Q moves towards Kc as the reaction runs: a small Q needs more products (forward), a large Q needs fewer products (backward), and equality means no further net change.
common_mistakes: Swapping the two cases. Small Q means too few products yet, so the reaction goes forward.
Forgetting the third case Q = Kc, which defines equilibrium.
steps.memory_tip: Q rises or falls until it equals Kc. Q below Kc means forward, Q above Kc means backward.
steps.margin_note: Write all three cases — the equality case is the definition of equilibrium.

insider_note: The second mark is the three-way comparison, so Q = Kc must be written alongside the two inequalities. Two cases out of three is a partial answer to the half of the question that carries the marks.
